newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds lose some earlier gains in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds lose some earlier gains in late trade.

text.p: Irish government bonds lost some of their earlier gains in thin late trade on Wednesday as a tired domestic market began to give away ground to UK gilts and German bunds, dealers said.

"The Irish market looked quite strong this morning on the back of good two-way interest and we saw it appreciate a little bit. But then it started to top out about mid-day as it just didn't have the legs to maintain the early pace. It has re-traced a bit since then," one dealer said.
"We have given a little ground to both the UK and Germany in the 10-year area in late trade," the dealer added.
By 1605 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had eased 25p from Tuesday's close to 102.25 to yield 5.87 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had eased 10 pence to 109.40 to yield 6.54 percent.
Dealers said U.S. Treasuries remained firm in busy late-morning trade after the November Chicago PMI was shown up to 57.6 and the November Michigan sentiment up at 99.2.
But they said flow was moderate in pre-holiday trade. The U.S. is closed for the Thanksgiving Holiday on Thursday.

In the UK, most of the British Treasury's panel of independent forecasters on Wednesday said they believed interest rates in Britain should still rise after finance minister Kenneth Clarke's budget on Tuesday. --Damien Lynch, Dublin newsroom 353-1-660-3377
